meta.title: Exposure Response: Contain Before Cleanup
meta.subtitle: Respond to a fictional Git secret-scanner finding using the priority that matches the credential state.
meta.role: Service owner responding to a finding

mission.objective: Reduce immediate credential risk first, verify the resulting state, then complete tracking and repository cleanup in the right order.

brief.role: You own a fictional service after a secret scanner reports a credential in Git history.
brief.context: The mission randomly presents an active or already-inactive credential case. Read the evidence carefully: the right response depends on whether the credential can still be used, but repository cleanup never substitutes for credential containment.
brief.safetyNote: Training data only. Every credential-looking value is fictional. Never replace a placeholder with a real credential in this simulation, an AI tool, a ticket, chat, email, log, screenshot or support message.

files.content: Teammate: I can rewrite the history now so the finding disappears. We can deal with the credential after the branch cleanup finishes.

briefOverride.context: The scanner finding is confirmed active in this mission. Reduce the time the credential remains usable, then complete the rest of the response.

choices.label: Rewrite Git history first so the value disappears from the repository
choices.feedback: History cleanup does not invalidate a credential that may already have been copied. Do not delay containment of an active credential.

choices.label: Rotate, revoke or disable the active credential through the approved process
choices.detail: Then verify the replacement and affected consumers before cleanup.

choices.label: Wait for the normal rotation schedule
choices.feedback: A confirmed active exposure requires event-driven response rather than waiting for a routine schedule.

items.text: Rotate, revoke or disable the exposed credential through the approved process
Verify the replacement and affected consumers
Document the remediation and update the approved finding workflow
Clean Git history and unnecessary branches after the credential is inactive

riskSignals.label: Repository history still contains exposed value

briefOverride.context: The service owner says the credential was already revoked before the scanner finding. Verify that status, complete tracking and clean the repository without pretending that deletion itself is revocation.

choices.label: Delete the commit and close the finding
choices.feedback: Deleting repository history does not prove that the credential is inactive.

choices.label: Verify that the credential is inactive, then document the finding and proceed with cleanup
choices.detail: The scenario already indicates prior revocation; verify rather than re-exposing the value.

choices.label: Paste the credential into a ticket so another team can test it
choices.feedback: Never move a suspected credential into a ticket to seek validation.

items.text: Verify that the credential is inactive
Document the status and update the approved finding workflow
Clean Git history and unnecessary branches when feasible

stages.title: Choose the first response action
stages.instruction: Use the scanner evidence and scenario status. Select the action that reduces risk without copying the credential into another system.

concept.label: Make an active exposed credential unusable before repository cleanup

hints: A repository edit changes where the value appears. Ask whether it changes whether the credential can be used.

feedback.correct: The first action matches the credential state in this scenario and does not confuse repository cleanup with credential containment.
feedback.incorrect: That action either delays containment, skips status verification or creates another exposure path.

stages.title: Put the remaining response actions in the safest order
stages.instruction: Arrange the actions so that immediate risk reduction and verification happen before repository cleanup.
hints: Repository cleanup matters, but it should not be allowed to delay credential containment or status verification.

feedback.correct: The sequence protects the credential boundary first, then completes evidence, tracking and repository cleanup.
feedback.incorrect: The order puts a later cleanup or tracking action ahead of the credential state that needs to be contained or verified.

feedbackByFirst.cleanup: History cleanup does not make an active credential unusable and does not verify that an inactive credential is truly inactive.

stages.title: Respond to the cleanup-first suggestion
stages.instruction: Choose the best response to the teammate message.

choices.label: Agree and finish history rewriting before addressing credential status
choices.feedback: Repository cleanup cannot replace credential containment or status verification.

choices.label: Keep credential containment or verified inactivity as the priority, then complete history cleanup
choices.detail: Do not let repository appearance drive the security response order.

choices.label: Ignore repository cleanup permanently because the credential has been handled
choices.feedback: Cleanup still matters after the credential risk is contained; it simply does not come first.

concept.label: Credential containment comes before repository cleanup

hints: The principle should stay the same even when a teammate is focused on making the finding disappear.

feedback.correct: You preserved the response priority when the same misconception reappeared in a team message.
feedback.incorrect: The response either puts cleanup too early or dismisses cleanup entirely.

completion.title: Exposure response contained
completion.message: You used the credential state to choose the right first action, kept repository cleanup in its proper place and reinforced the priority when it reappeared later in the workflow.
takeaways: A scanner finding is a signal to investigate; this mission tells you whether the simulated credential is active or already inactive.
For an active exposed credential, make it unusable before history cleanup.
For an already-inactive credential, verify the status, document it and then clean repository history when feasible.
Never copy a suspected credential into tickets, chat or AI tools to seek validation.
